desc: pretest prevalence of PE among ED/outpatients formally worked up for SUSPECTED PE (the base rate before any test)
D-dimer above the assay cutoff (highly sensitive quantitative ELISA)
objective clinical signs/symptoms of DVT (leg swelling + pain on palpation of deep veins) — a Wells criterion
PE judged as likely as or more likely than any alternative diagnosis — the Wells gestalt criterion
tachycardia, heart rate > 100/min — a Wells criterion
immobilization >=3 days or surgery in the previous 4 weeks — a Wells criterion
previously objectively diagnosed DVT or PE — a Wells criterion
malignancy on treatment, treated within 6 months, or palliative — a Wells criterion
CT pulmonary angiography showing an intraluminal filling defect (the confirmatory test)
CT pulmonary angiography negative for PE on an adequate study
